source_text: Apostoli me testimonium praetermisisse confingis, quod nec tibi opitulari potest, et a me praetermissum non est; sed eo insertum ordine, quo a te fuerat collocatum; utque in primo fideliter commemoratum, ita enim in quarto operis mei libro, licet cursim et breviter, explanatum est [n20] . Commemorationem quoque catholicae Ecclesiae, quam tu ad hoc feceras, ut catholicam fidem desererent a te decepti, et catholica miserabiles appellatione gauderent, non praetermisi. Et quamvis nulla argumentorum vis in eiusmodi verbis esset, tamen a me haud aliter dictorum tuorum caput propositum est, quam a te fuerat ordinatum. Lege editos libros meos responsionisque fidem, quam tu arguis fraudis, aspiciens, me interim pronuntia vera dicere; tu vero, si consuetudo tua permiserit, erubesce. Sed iam ostensa inexcusabili falsitate, quae semper quidem turpis, fit tamen turpior cum locum censoris invadit, et deformitatem suam decori exprobrat alieno; responde, quid Manichaeis sensibus aut nomen Ecclesiae aut Apostoli verba conducant, ut ea cum tam magna invidia praetermissa causeris?
pass_a_gloss: You invent that I passed over the testimony of the Apostle, which both cannot help you, and has not been passed over by me; but inserted in that order in which it had been placed by you; and as it was faithfully recalled in the first, so indeed in the fourth book of my work, though in passing and briefly, it has been explained. The recalling also of the catholic Church, which you had made for this, that those deceived by you might desert the catholic faith and, miserable, rejoice in the catholic naming, I did not pass over. And although there was no force of arguments in words of that kind, nevertheless the head of your sayings was set out by me not otherwise than it had been ordered by you. Read my published books and, looking at the faith of the answer, which you charge with fraud, pronounce me for now to speak true things; but you, if your custom will have permitted, blush. But now, with inexcusable falsehood shown, which is always indeed base, yet becomes baser when it invades the place of the censor and casts its own deformity in the teeth of another's comeliness; answer, what the name of the Church or the Apostle's words contribute to Manichaean senses, that you should complain with so great ill-will that they were passed over?

pass_b_english: You invent the charge that I omitted the apostle's testimony, although it cannot help you and I did not omit it. I inserted it in the same order in which you had placed it. Just as I faithfully quoted it in the first book of my work, I also explained it in the fourth, though briefly and in passing (compare Augustine, Against Julian 6.75). Nor did I omit your mention of the catholic Church, which you had made so that those you deceived would abandon the catholic faith and yet, poor wretches, rejoice in the catholic name. Although words of that sort had no argumentative force, I nevertheless presented the opening of your statement exactly as you had arranged it. Read my published books; see the faithfulness of my reply, which you accuse of fraud; and for the present admit that I am speaking the truth. As for you, blush, if your habitual conduct will allow it. Your inexcusable falsehood has now been exposed. Falsehood is always disgraceful, but becomes more disgraceful when it usurps the censor's place and reproaches another person's beauty with its own ugliness. Answer, then: how does either the Church's name or the apostle's language benefit Manichaean ideas, that you should make so inflammatory a complaint about their omission?

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian claims the catholic faith against Augustine; keep lowercase-c catholic as the universal church, not a later confessional brand.
